# `flavorizr.lock`

`flavorizr.lock` is the memory of what flutter_flavorizr applied to a project.
It lives in the root of the project and **is meant to be committed**: it lets a
run remove what an earlier run generated (for example a flavor that was dropped
from the configuration) and tell a change made by the tool from one made by
hand.

It is written only after a run fully succeeded, and never edited by hand.

## Example

```yaml
# flavorizr.lock: generated by flutter_flavorizr, do not edit.
# Commit this file: it lets flavorizr remove what it generated.
flavorizrVersion: 3.0.0
flavors:
  dev: sha256:5f2c0a
  prod: sha256:91be44
processors:
  android:buildGradle:
    files:
      android/app/build.gradle:
        hash: sha256:7a1d02
        ownership: patched
  flutter:flavors:
    files:
      lib/flavors.g.dart:
        hash: sha256:c3d9f1
        ownership: managed
      lib/flavors.dart:
        ownership: scaffold
  ios:xcodeproj:
    objects:
      ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:
        - 97C146E61CF9000F007C117D
        - A1B2C3D4E5F60718293A4B5C
  ios:plist:
    keys:
      ios/Runner/Info.plist:
        CFBundleDisplayName: sha256:0d44ab
  android:icons:
    inputs:
      android/app/src/dev/res/mipmap-hdpi/ic_launcher.png: sha256:e8a6b7
schemaVersion: 1
```

## Schema (version 1)

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | integer | Version of the lock format. Bumped when the format changes in a way an older flavorizr cannot read. |
| `flavorizrVersion` | string | Version of flutter_flavorizr that wrote the lock. |
| `flavors` | map | Flavor name to the hash of its resolved configuration. The names are what the engine reads back as `previousFlavors`. |
| `processors` | map | Processor id (for example `android:buildGradle`) to what it owns. |

Each processor has these optional sections, left out when empty:

| Section | Shape | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | path to `{ownership, hash?}` | Whole files. `ownership` is `scaffold`, `managed` or `patched`. `hash` is the hash of the owned content (the whole file for `managed`, the owned parts for `patched`) and is present exactly for the hashed classes, so never for `scaffold`. |
| `regions` | path to region id to hash | Marked regions of a shared file. |
| `keys` | path to key to hash | Owned keys of a plist, manifest or XML file. |
| `objects` | path to list of UUIDs | pbxproj object UUIDs, sorted. |
| `inputs` | output path to hash | Generated binaries such as icons: the hash of the *inputs* (source file hash plus options), never of the output, so bumping a library such as `image` creates no noise. |

Notes:

* Artifacts of the `local` ownership class are **never** stored: they are
  regenerated silently on every run and are neither drift nor conflict.
* Hashes are opaque strings. The engine decides how they are computed (the
  recommended spelling is `<algorithm>:<hex digest>`, such as `sha256:...`).
* Paths are relative to the project root and use `/`.
* `flavors` and `processors` are required on read, the sections of a processor
  are optional. Unknown keys at the same `schemaVersion` are ignored on read.
* A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is tolerated on read.
* **`project.pbxproj`.** The Xcode project of a platform is shared by every
  Darwin processor (`xcodeproj:ios`, `xcodeproj:macos`) and is a `patched`
  file, so the lock hashes only the part of it the processors own, which is told
  by `EngineResource(..., ownedContent: {path: reader})`. For now that part is
  what `ios:xcconfig` and `macos:configs` write: the file references to the
  flavor xcconfigs (`Flutter/<flavor>Debug.xcconfig` and `Runner/Configs/...`,
  and the `Profile` and `Release` ones, for any flavor) and their entries in a
  Resources phase, which a run removes. An edit of the
  rest, by Xcode, CocoaPods, Flutter or a 2.x processor, is not drift. **Known
  limitation:** the owned build settings (#515) and the UUIDs of the objects the
  other processors create (#516) are not part of it yet, so an edit of them is
  not seen as drift either; whatever a processor that is not ported changes
  stays out of the lock.

## Determinism

The same logical content is always written to the same bytes, so two runs with
no changes produce a byte-identical lock and merge conflicts stay small. The
lock records `flavorizrVersion`, so the bytes are identical for the same
flutter_flavorizr version: upgrading the tool rewrites that one line.

* every mapping is written with its keys sorted by code unit, and the lists of
  `objects` are sorted;
* two spaces of indentation, `\n` line endings, UTF-8 without BOM, a single
  trailing newline, the same header comment;
* empty sections are left out, and an empty top-level section is written as
  `{}`;
* scalars are plain when that is safe and double quoted otherwise, so a value
  such as `yes`, `1e3` or `a: b` stays a string;
* nothing depends on the time, the machine or the order the content was
  collected in.

The lock is written to a temporary file next to it and then renamed, so an
interrupted write never leaves a truncated lock.

## Version guard

When it reads the lock, flutter_flavorizr checks, before anything else:

* a `schemaVersion` **higher** than the one it writes: the run is blocked, since
  the format is unknown, with a hint to upgrade flutter_flavorizr;
* a `flavorizrVersion` **higher** than the running one (semantic version
  precedence, build metadata ignored): the run is blocked with the same hint,
  since the newer version may have recorded things this one would drop;
* anything older or equal is read normally. Version 1 is the only format so
  far; when it changes, the new reader is responsible for the older versions.

A lock that is not valid YAML or does not have the shape above is reported as
malformed, with the file to restore from version control or delete.

## In code

* `FlavorizrLock`, `ProcessorLock` and `LockedFile` (`lib/src/engine/lock/`)
  are the plain data model. `LockedFile` refuses a `local` file and enforces
  the hash rule above.
* `LockCodec.encode` / `LockCodec.decode` convert to and from text, in memory.
* `LockStore` reads and writes the file in the project root.
